name: MathlibAnnex.exists_aeConstantOn_of_local
title: From local to global almost-everywhere constancy

content.display_title: From local to global almost-everywhere constancy
content.one_sentence_role: Separates agreement of constants by connectedness from countable measure-theoretic gluing.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space with a measurable structure, and let $\mu$ be positive on every nonempty open set. Let $Y$ be any set, $u:X\to Y$, and let $U\subseteq X$ be connected and Lindelöf. Suppose that for every $x\in U$ there are an open neighborhood $V_x$ and a constant $c_x\in Y$ such that
$$x\in V_x\subseteq U,\qquad u=c_x\quad\mu|_{V_x}\text{-almost everywhere}.$$
Then there is one $c\in Y$ with $u=c$ almost everywhere for $\mu|_U$.
content.assumptions: Here connected means nonempty and admitting no partition into two disjoint nonempty relatively open subsets. Lindelöf means that every open cover of $U$ admits a countable subcover. No finiteness or Haar assumption is imposed on $\mu$, and $X$ need not be second countable. No topology or measurable structure on the value set $Y$ is required. The supplied neighborhoods in particular make $U$ open, although openness is not a separate input.
content.conclusion: One common constant works outside a null set for the restricted measure on $U$. Connectedness identifies the local constants; Lindelöf supplies the countability needed to join their exceptional sets. Those are distinct uses of the hypotheses.
content.proof_summary: Fix a constant from one local neighborhood. Its region of local validity and its complement in $U$ are disjoint open sets. Connectedness makes that region all of $U$. Select a countable subcover of neighborhoods carrying this same constant and apply countable gluing.

proof_steps.text:
**Fix a value and its region.** Choose $x_0\in U$ and its local data $(V_0,c_0)$. Define
$$G:=\{x\in U:\ \exists V\text{ open},\ x\in V\subseteq U,
\ u=c_0\ \mu|_V\text{-almost everywhere}\}.$$
It contains $x_0$. It is open: a witnessing $V$ for $x$ is contained in $G$, because the same $V$ witnesses membership for every point of $V$.

**Show the complementary region is open.** For $x\in U\setminus G$, choose local data $(V_x,c_x)$. If some $y\in V_x$ were also in $G$, take a witnessing open set $W$ for $y$ with constant $c_0$. Then $y\in V_x\cap W$, so this open overlap has positive measure. [The open-overlap theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/MeasureTheory/Function/AEConstant.lean#L92-L105) gives $c_x=c_0$. But $(V_x,c_x)$ would then witness $x\in G$, a contradiction. Thus
$$x\in V_x\subseteq U\setminus G,$$
and $U\setminus G$ is open.

**Use connectedness to identify the region.** The disjoint open sets $G$ and $U\setminus G$ cover $U$. Preconnectedness forces $U$ to lie in one of them. It cannot lie in the latter because $x_0\in G\subseteq U$. Hence $G=U$. In particular, every point of $U$ now has an open neighborhood on which the same $c_0$ works almost everywhere.

**Use a countable cover to glue.** Choose for each $x\in U$ one of these neighborhoods $V_x$. Lindelöf gives a countable set $T\subseteq U$ of indices such that
$$U\subseteq\bigcup_{x\in T}V_x,\qquad
u=c_0\quad\mu|_{V_x}\text{-almost everywhere for each }x\in T.$$
[The countable-cover gluing theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/MeasureTheory/Function/AEConstant.lean#L24-L47) gives $u=c_0$ almost everywhere for $\mu|_U$. Only this selected countable family is used in the measure argument; the original uncountable family of local null sets is never united.

content.lean_realization_notes: The local data at $x$ are an open set $V$, the relations $x\in V\subseteq U$, and a value $c\in Y$ satisfying $u=c$ almost everywhere for $\mu|_V$. At one chosen point of the nonempty set $U$, these data supply the initial value $c_0\in Y$. Thus no separate nonemptiness assumption on $Y$ is needed.
